newsitem.title: UK: Watchdog yet to decide on Centrica price cut.
newsitem.headline: Watchdog yet to decide on Centrica price cut.

text.p: British gas industry regulator Ofgas has still to decide whether it will give the green light to the price discount scheme gas supplier Centrica introduced earlier on Tuesday in the south west of England.
The watchdog will approve the scheme if it finds that competition in the domestic gas market in Cornwall, Devon and Somerset has been fully established.
To reach its decision, Ofgas will consult other gas suppliers and the Gas Consumer Council. The consultation period can last up to 28 days.
"We will put out consultation letters either today or tomorrow," an Ofgas spokesman said.
Centrica will have to withdraw its ValuePlus discount scheme if Ofgas decides competition has not been fully established.

ValuePlus is available to customers who choose to pay by monthly direct debit and are prepared to stay with Centrica, which still markets its products under the British Gas brand name, for a minimum 12 months.
The domestic gas market in England's south western counties was introduced in April last year and saw the market share of former monopoly Centrica fall by about 20 percent since then.
A second pilot area, covering Dorset and the former county of Avon, started last month. Three other counties in southern England will be opened up on March 7.
The Gas Consumers Council said it could sympathise with Centrica's planned move to stave off rivals, but added the price cut of up to 12 percent could be judged as premature.
